issues.title: Confidence gate threshold (alpha) too conservative at 0.3
issues.description: The alpha=0.3 threshold meant MI correction only activated when the model was very uncertain (max token probability < 0.3). Analysis showed the successful Qwen2.5-VL generality check effectively used constant correction (always active). Hyperparameter sweeps on 200-300 MMStar items tested alpha values {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0} and found alpha=0.8 performed best. This makes the correction active whenever the model isn't highly confident (max_p < 0.8), which covers most generation steps. Full run with alpha=0.8 improved MMStar from 61.93% to 62.07% (+0.14pp) and HallusionBench from 67.67% to 67.76% (+0.09pp).

issues.title: Lambda confirmed optimal at 0.005
issues.description: Swept lambda values {0.005, 0.01, 0.02} on 200 MMStar items. lambda=0.005 achieved 60.50% vs vanilla 59.00% (+1.50pp), while higher lambda values (0.01: 59.00%, 0.02: 60.00%) performed worse. The gradual weight ramp of lambda=0.005 is necessary for long-CoT (avg ~140 tokens think block) to avoid overwhelming the model's reasoning process.

summary: Optimized the confidence gate threshold alpha from 0.3 to 0.8 based on systematic hyperparameter sweeps. This makes MI correction active for more generation steps, improving both benchmarks: MMStar 61.93% -> 62.07% (now only -0.06pp vs vanilla 62.13%, essentially neutral) and HallusionBench 67.67% -> 67.76% (best across all methods, +1.51pp vs vanilla). The improvement is modest but moves MMStar from a slight negative (-0.20pp) to essentially neutral (-0.06pp), demonstrating that MI decoding can counteract visual forgetting without degrading general visual reasoning.
